starter_metadata.title: Evaluating LLM Agent Collusion in Double Auctions
starter_metadata.summary: LLM sellers in a continuous double auction coordinate to keep prices high. Communication, an overseer, urgency pressure and the choice of model all change how much they collude.

starter_metadata.title: Adaptive Algorithms and Collusion via Coupling
starter_metadata.summary: Identifies 'spontaneous coupling', a statistical linkage between learners' estimates that yields supracompetitive play even for memoryless algorithms unable to punish. Frames collusion as statistical dependence, which suits information-theoretic detection.
starter_metadata.source: literature search: economics, law and policy

starter_metadata.title: Information-Theoretic Approach to Detect Collusion in Multi-Agent Games
starter_metadata.summary: Defines a measure of collusion based on statistical dependence between agents' actions that applies to arbitrary multi-agent games. The reference point for information-theoretic detection.

starter_metadata.title: Artificial Intelligence, Algorithmic Pricing, and Collusion
starter_metadata.summary: Q-learning agents in a repeated logit Bertrand market learn supracompetitive prices backed by finite punishments after deviations. The foundational environment reused by most LLM pricing-collusion papers, with deviation impulse responses as the evidence standard.
starter_metadata.source: literature search: economics, law and policy

entries.title: Supracompetitive Pricing Under AI Monoculture
entries.identity_audit_row: | Cao & Hu 2026 | [v3 §1](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.01279v3) | shared-advisor theoretical model; no seller communication, not absence of coordination |

starter_metadata.title: Supracompetitive Pricing Under AI Monoculture
starter_metadata.summary: Duopoly model where sellers take pricing advice from a shared LLM. Correlated recommendations plus model updates that aggregate seller feedback produce supracompetitive prices without coordination, linking LLM monoculture to hub-and-spoke theories.
starter_metadata.source: literature search: economics, law and policy

starter_metadata.summary: LLM pricing agents (GPT-4) in a repeated oligopoly quickly reach prices above the competitive level without being told to collude, and small changes to prompt wording move prices substantially.

starter_metadata.title: Noncooperative Collusion under Imperfect Price Information
starter_metadata.summary: Models collusion as a noncooperative equilibrium sustained by trigger-strategy price wars under imperfect monitoring. The template for the reward-punishment definition of collusion used in most algorithmic-collusion work.
starter_metadata.source: literature search: economics, law and policy

starter_metadata.title: Strategic Collusion of LLM Agents: Market Division in Multi-Commodity Competitions
starter_metadata.summary: LLM agents competing across several commodities divide the market between them, each specialising, without explicit instruction. Shows collusion through actions rather than messages.

starter_metadata.title: Hidden in Plain Text: Emergence & Mitigation of Steganographic Collusion in LLMs
starter_metadata.authors: Mathew, Matthews, McCarthy, Velja, Schroeder de Witt, Cope & Schoots
starter_metadata.summary: Shows steganographic collusion can emerge without instruction under optimisation pressure (gradient-based and in-context RL). Standard mitigations, passive oversight and paraphrasing, are shown to be non-robust.
starter_metadata.source: literature search: AI safety and multi-agent ML

starter_metadata.title: Secret Collusion among AI Agents: Multi-Agent Deception via Steganography
starter_metadata.authors: Motwani, Baranchuk, Strohmeier, Bolina, Torr, Hammond & Schroeder de Witt
starter_metadata.summary: Defines secret collusion as agents using steganography to hide unauthorised coordination from oversight. Introduces the CASE evaluation framework, measures how stego capability scales across models, and analyses limits of mitigations such as paraphrasing and channel restrictions.
starter_metadata.source: literature search: AI safety and multi-agent ML

starter_metadata.summary: Detects collusion from the internal activations of several agents at once using interpretability probes. Defines collusion as communication within a subgroup that leads to actions harmful to outsiders.

starter_metadata.title: Emergent Collusion in Long-Horizon LLM Agent Interaction
starter_metadata.summary: Two agents verify each other's work over repeated episodes where higher reward requires breaking the protocol. Collusion emerges without instruction in 94% of trajectories across 10 models, sooner for more capable models, driven by peer behaviour and history.
starter_metadata.source: literature search: AI safety and multi-agent ML

starter_metadata.title: Audit the Whisper: Detecting Steganographic Collusion in Multi-Agent LLMs
